transactions.notes: Seed confirmed. MLB.com (team/league release) confirms KSE is buying Moreno's controlling interest, with Moreno keeping an undisclosed minority stake; close expected Q1 2027 pending MLB approval. The $4B valuation (an MLB record) is not official: it comes from The Athletic (Britt Ghiroli), repeated by CBS, Yahoo and MLBTR. The exact % acquired is undisclosed. CBS's '100%' is wrong per MLB.com.

transactions.buyer: José E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones (Feliciano is control person); minority partners incl. Joey and Jesse Buss
transactions.notes: Seed corrected on dates: the agreement was announced May 2, 2026 (after an Apr 22 report in The Athletic), not 'early 2026'. MLB owners approved unanimously Aug 17, 2026. A team release titled 'Sale of Padres successfully completed' followed, and the owners were introduced Aug 24; the exact closing date was not captured. The buyers get control with about 40% of the equity (ESPN, The Athletic); the Seidler family keeps some equity. $3.9B is the reported valuation (an MLB record at the time).

transactions.buyer: Group led by Patrick Zalupski (with Ken Babby and others)
transactions.notes: dateAnnounced is June 18, 2025, when the Rays confirmed exclusive talks. An agreement in principle was reported in July 2025 without a precise date. Approved Sept 22 and closed Sept 30, 2025. $1.7B is reported, not official. Sternberg kept a minority stake, reported at about 10% (so ~90% sold; approximate). The deal includes the USL Tampa Bay Rowdies.

transactions.buyer: David Rubenstein and Michael Arougheti-led group (incl. Cal Ripken Jr., Mike Bloomberg, Grant Hill)
transactions.notes: The $1.725B covers the franchise plus the Orioles' stake in MASN. The group bought about 40% at first, with the Angelos family's ~30% to be bought later; existing LPs have tag-along rights. Owners approved on Wednesday, Mar 27, 2024 (the Banner print says Mar 26, but that was a Tuesday). The sale was finalized within days of Peter Angelos's death on Mar 23.

transactions.buyer: Glick Family Investments, George G. Hicks, Craig Leipold
transactions.notes: The Pohlads ended their control-sale process in Aug 2025 and brought in LPs instead. The Dec 17, 2025 announcement: just over 20% at a reported $1.75B (The Athletic, Dan Hayes), about $350M, used to pay down roughly $400-500M of debt. The valuation is reported, not official. Closing and MLB approval dates were not confirmed.

transactions.buyer: Justin Ishbia (with Mat and Jeff Ishbia)
transactions.notes: Reported Feb-Mar 2025 (The Athletic, Sportico): a majority of White Sox LPs agreed to sell their shares to Ishbia at a $1.8B valuation. The % is undisclosed. dateAnnounced is a report date, not a formal announcement. The June 5, 2025 agreement adds capital infusions in 2025-26 and a control option from 2029-2034; that option is not a sale (see rejected).

Sportico reported that about 15% was sold 'this spring' (2026) at $1.55B; another source put it closer to $1.4B. Proceeds (~$233M) went to debt paydown. The 2026-06-01 date is Sportcal's publication date; the exact deal date is undisclosed. Sportcal appears to follow Sportico, so the two sources may not be fully independent.

ESPN and LVSportsBiz confirm the stake; the % is undisclosed. CNBC (Mike Ozanian) reported about $50M at a ~$3.8B post-money valuation, as cited by Sportcal. That valuation covers the A's and the new Las Vegas ballpark, so it is not comparable to team-only values (Forbes: ~$2B). Part of Fisher's ~$550M raise for the stadium. MLB approval status is unclear.

transactions.seller: Steinbrenner family and some YGE limited partners
transactions.notes: A $2.6B debt-plus-equity deal into Yankee Global Enterprises, which holds the Yankees, YES Network, Legends, and stakes in NYCFC and AC Milan; it is not a team-only valuation. Sportico: YGE valued at more than $10B, with the Steinbrenners selling at least 4%. NY Post (Gasparino): 'significantly' more than $12B, with Apollo taking 8% common now plus 8% convertible preferred (16% total). Valuation and stake are uncertain; the equity piece still needs MLB to waive its private-equity cap.

transactions.buyer: Brett Jefferson, Marc Grandisson, Bobby Farnham
transactions.notes: Seed corrected: the three buyers were named when the club announced them on Mar 12, 2026 (Jefferson, Grandisson and ex-NHL player Farnham), so they are not undisclosed. The 12.5% at $2.66B (Sportico) is confirmed. NHL owners approved on 'Tuesday' (Sportico), which I dated to Mar 10, 2026 (the Tuesday before the Mar 12 announcement). Sportico said it had not closed yet as of then.

transactions.buyer: Hoffmann Family of Companies (David Hoffmann family)
transactions.notes: ~US$1.7B was reported by Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman and is not official. FSG paid ~$900M in 2021. The NHL Board of Governors approved unanimously (Florida Weekly; exact date not captured). Wikipedia says the Hoffmanns took full control June 23, 2026 and lists Mario Lemieux as a remaining minority owner, so stakePct is left null.

Seed corrected: C$4.7B for BCE's 37.5% of MLSE was announced Sept 18, 2024 and closed July 1, 2025 (CBC), not July 2024. This took Rogers from co-owner to 75% control. Entity is MLSE (Leafs, Raptors, TFC, Argos, Marlies, Scotiabank Arena), not the Leafs alone. Implied 100% value C$12.53B, converted at 0.73586 USD/CAD (ECB reference rate via frankfurter.app, 2024-09-18). Rogers funded it partly with a private investor, amount not stated.

Rogers is buying the last 25% of MLSE for C$4.35B, which implies C$17.4B for 100%; close expected Q4 2026 pending league approvals. Entity is MLSE (Leafs, Raptors, TFC, Argos, Marlies, arena). Converted at 0.70307 USD/CAD (ECB reference rate via frankfurter.app, 2026-07-06). Rogers also said it plans to sell a minority stake in its combined sports/media assets within a year (not agreed).

transactions.buyer: Smith Entertainment Group (Ryan and Ashley Smith)
transactions.seller: NHL / Alex Meruelo (Arizona Coyotes hockey assets)
transactions.notes: Structured as a new franchise, not a sale: Smith paid a $1.2B 'expansion' fee and got the Coyotes' hockey assets (roster, reserve list, picks, hockey ops). The NHL paid Meruelo $1B; the $200M gap was effectively a relocation fee shared by the other clubs. Meruelo kept the Coyotes name and a 5-year reactivation right. NHL.com confirms the structure but not the prices, which come from Wikipedia and Bloomberg. Team now called Utah Mammoth.

rejected.description: Michael Andlauer bought control from the Melnyk estate (~US$950M reported); purchase agreement June 2023, completed Sept 21, 2023.
rejected.reason: Outside the 36-month control comp window: closed Sept 21, 2023, three days before the 2023-09-24 cutoff.

rejected.description: June 5, 2025 framework: Reinsdorf may sell control to Justin Ishbia in 2029-2033, with Ishbia holding an option after the 2034 season.
rejected.reason: Not agreed: a future option, not a control sale. The team says there is 'no assurance' it will happen. The related LP share purchases are listed as a minority transaction.

rejected.description: Pohlad family control-sale process (Allen & Co., Oct 2024 to Aug 2025). Justin Ishbia was the leading bidder but withdrew in Feb 2025.
rejected.reason: Not agreed: the sale process ended Aug 13, 2025. The Pohlads kept control and sold ~20% to LPs instead (listed as a transaction).

rejected.description: David Blitzer's 2022 purchase of 25% came with an option to take majority control around 2028. The owner's brief mentioned Dolan-Haslam, but no Haslam involvement with the Guardians was found.
rejected.reason: Not agreed: the option has not been exercised and the 2022 stake predates the window. No Dolan-Haslam deal found.

rejected.team: Toronto Blue Jays / Rogers sports assets
rejected.description: Rogers said (July 2026) it plans to sell a minority stake in its combined sports, media and entertainment assets (Blue Jays, MLSE, Sportsnet) within the next year.
rejected.reason: Not agreed: a stated intention only, with no buyer or terms.

unverified.description: Tampa Bay Lightning: Vinik Sports Group sold a majority stake to a group led by Doug Ostrover and Marc Lipschultz (Blue Owl co-CEOs). NHL approved Oct 1, 2024; finalized Oct 24, 2024; control passes to Ostrover/Lipschultz after ~3 years. This is a control sale inside the 36-month window. Sources: https://www.nhl.com/lightning/news/jeff-vinik-announces-expansion-of-tampa-bay-lightning-ownership-group and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_Vinik

unverified.description: San Francisco Giants: Sixth Street bought ~10% (Mar 18, 2025), with proceeds going to Oracle Park, spring training and Mission Rock. Sources: https://www.sportcal.com/news/san-francisco-giants-sell-10-stake-to-sixth-street/ , https://pitchbook.com/news/articles/sixth-street-partners-acquires-stake-in-san-francisco-giants , https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-03-18/san-francisco-giants-sells-10-stake-to-sixth-street-partners
unverified.whatWasMissing: Deal valuation: no financial terms disclosed. The $4.2B (Sportico) and $3.8B (Forbes) figures in coverage are outlet estimates, not deal values.

Source: https://komonews.com/news/local/melinda-french-gates-joining-kraken-ownership-fueling-nba-expansion-talk

Sources: https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/49460092/chan-ho-park-becomes-first-korean-buy-stake-mlb-club-joining-athletics-group and https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2026/jul/27/chan-ho-park-becomes-1st-korean-buy-stake-mlb-club-joining-athletics/
